[0] everyday_reading (E): Everyday "chain" of events suggests the whole history matters; in a Markov chain the next state depends only on the current state, through that state's row of the transition matrix.
[1] misconception (M) -> StartPageMatters: wrong rule: The page ranks depend on which page the surfer starts from. Right rule: For the random-surfer chain the long-run probabilities are the same for all starting pages (basic limit theorem); that is why RandomSurfer can start at page 0.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> StartPageMatters: Applies LT (each step uses the row of the current state) unevenly: e.g. on some steps using the starting page's row instead of the current page's row. (here mixing in: "The page ranks depend on which page the surfer starts from")

[0] names_the_element (N): A mathematical model: a random process on states (pages) whose moves are given by a transition matrix.
[1] states_the_rule (S): The surfer's random process is a Markov chain; by the basic limit theorem the probability of eventually ending on any page is the same for all starting pages (mixing), though not all chains mix.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): State sequence: from the current page i, choose the next page j with probability p[i][j]; repeat from j. In probability form, the t-step distribution is the (t-1)-step distribution times the matrix.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Produces the stationary probabilities (page ranks): for tiny.txt about .27 .27 .15 .25 .07.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): One step moves the state from page i to a page j drawn from row i; in matrix form, one multiplication turns the distribution after t-1 moves into the distribution after t moves.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): The chain is defined by the matrix: it must be square with every row a probability distribution.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): Each vector-matrix multiplication advances the chain's probabilities by one move; repeating it approaches the stationary vector.
[2] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Model a memoryless random process to compute its long-run behaviour (page ranks) instead of following one surfer.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> StartPageMatters: Changing the start state keeps the limiting distribution (if the chain mixes); removing the random leap can break mixing; squaring the matrix gives two-step probabilities.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Right model when the next state depends only on the current state with fixed probabilities (web surfing, many random processes); its limit theorem gives start-independent results only for chains that mix.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Each row must be a probability distribution. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: A non-stochastic row (sum not 1, e.g. dangling page or bad scaling): simulation and multiplication give wrong probabilities.
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The chain must mix for start-independent ranks. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: No random leap and a spider trap: the surfer gets stuck and results depend on where it starts.
